sections.title: Form and habitat
sections.text: A large epiphytic bromeliad of wet tropical forests, native from southern Mexico through Central America. When flowering it reaches about 1–2 m; its rosette leaves may measure 80–140 cm and have strongly toothed margins. A long branched inflorescence bears yellow flowers; ripe berries are pale cream to yellow and about 1–2 cm across.

sections.title: Uses and image note
sections.text: The sources consulted establish no food use or toxicity. The plant and inflorescence in the existing plate are broadly plausible, but the dark blue-black berry shown conflicts with botanical records describing pale ripe berries. Unlike the terrestrial cultivated pineapple, this species is epiphytic and has small berries rather than a large fused fruit.
